text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Thailand takes a bold step to cure its ailing economy by floating baht in surprise move regarded by analysts as defacto devaluation of currency.
- China's top leaders call for concrete steps towards complete reunification of country in renewed campaign aimed at Taiwan following Hongkong's successful return to Chinese sovereignty.
- Departed British governor of Hongkong Chris Patten is to profit from territory's handover to China by 350,000 pounds sterling, the Times newspaper says.
- Egyptian teenager who complained of stomach pains was found to have underdeveloped twin foetus lodged above abdomen where it had been slowly feeding off him for past 16 years, medical sources say.
- Cash trading of Thai baht grinds to halt at most banks but people could still sell currency for Singapore dollars to money changers at sharply lower rates reflecting baht's decline.
- Travellers buying baht at Changi Airport pay between Singapore $5.67 and S$5.64 for 100 baht at money changing counters of two Singapore banks -- only marginally lower than previous day's rates.
- Mainboard-listed Chemical Industries (Far East) bags 11 prime freehold London commercial properties for S$96.8 million from National Westminster Bank Group, one of Britain's big four banks.
- U.S Federal Reserve decides to hold interest rates steady amid signs economic growth has slowed from sizzling first quarter pace.
- U.S President Bill Clinton recommends Internet be declared "free-trade zone" without taxation, and calls for global agreement on matter within 12 months.

- HMI Balestier Hospital, which has entered into healthcare alliance with renowned U.S. Massachusetts General Hospital, plans to list on local bourse in 1999 or 2000 to raise funds for regional expansion.
- Jurong Engineering Ltd lands new contracts in Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia worth more than S$40 million.
